items.question: Who checks the Verifiable Intent chain in a live Agent Pay authorization, and how?
items.context: Partly answered by two announcements. Travelport, Booked AI, Basis Theory and Mastercard said on 2026-11-12 that VI linked a customer's approval to a live flight purchase and that a mismatch would have stopped the payment, and Mastercard said on 2026-11-19 that a coffee an agent bought on the consumer's pre-captured intent, with acceptance through Antom, ran on Agent Pay with VI. Neither release names VI layers or a mode or says whether the network, the merchant or another party checked the chain; Mastercard says it is embedding VI into the payment flow, but its VI API specifications are not public (as of 2026-11-21).

items.question: Is the ChatGPT Wallet token a Mastercard Agentic Token issued under Agent Pay, and does Mastercard require agent registration or Web Bot Auth for it?
items.context: OpenAI says the payment network provides a payment token, but names no program (2026-11-13). As read 2026-11-21 its post names American Express, Chase, Mastercard and Visa as partners, where the launch-day text named three; Chase takes part as a card issuer whose cardholders approve the connection in the Chase app. Mastercard's CEO said on 2026-04-30 that the deepening OpenAI partnership reinforces OpenAI's use of Agent Pay, and on 2026-10-29 that a strategic OpenAI partnership includes the use of Agent Pay (both reported); neither remark names the program behind Wallet tokens. ChatGPT's cloud browser signs certain requests with Web Bot Auth as https://chatgpt.com, and OpenAI does not document the tag.

items.question: Where is the Mastercard key directory, and how are keys rotated and delisted?
items.context: The only host in the docs did not resolve on 2026-10-21; Cloudflare said in 2025-10 that each network would host a directory; rotation and delisting are undocumented.

items.question: Who carries the loss when an agent buys the wrong thing within its limits?
items.context: No public agent-specific reason codes or liability shift; Mastercard's public rules defer to Agent Pay Program Standards that are not public. An unattributed answer in VI issue 15 says liability work is ongoing.

items.question: Can a Verifiable Intent Autonomous mandate satisfy PSD2 SCA when the user is absent?
items.context: VI says it gives a cryptographic form of dynamic linking but does not replace SCA; no regulator has addressed it.

items.question: Will Verifiable Intent fix the duplicate-digest conflict with RFC 9901?
items.context: Issue 29 has been open since 2026-07-17 with no maintainer response, and the repository has had no commits since 2026-04-20.

items.question: How reliably do authorization messages mark agent involvement?
items.context: The probability score rolling out for US testing (announced 2026-09-30) implies agent involvement is not always marked; its fields and thresholds are unpublished.

items.question: How will Mastercard's tag and directory align with the IETF Web Bot Auth draft?
items.context: Mastercard uses its own tag, while the working group draft requires web-bot-auth. Since revision -01 (2026-10-29) the draft also makes each Signature-Agent value the URL of a JWK Set and requires the dictionary form of the header, while Mastercard's example sends a quoted directory origin. No alignment plan is published.

items.question: What does Agent Pay for Machines settle on, and at what cost?
items.context: Mastercard's 2026-10-20 brief describes a pilot flow built on x402 with signed off-chain vouchers, Base settlement and BVNK as the agent wallet, but publishes no pricing, contract addresses or settlement schedule.
